transcript:
Meeting: Edge Onramp: SDK Auth & Optimize Lab (Python/TS)
Date: 2025-11-21 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lena (AeroScale), Omar (AeroScale), Priya (AeroScale)
Shared links: https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/edge-onramp, https://redwood.ai/docs/soc2, https://redwood.ai/optimize/recommendations, spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-benchmarks

Summary:
Quick onboarding walkthrough of the SDKs (Python & TypeScript), auth patterns (API key vs SSO/SAML), sandbox provisioning, and a short demo of Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Customer wanted to validate security posture and run a latency benchmark on a sample prompt set next week.

Topics:
- SDK install and examples (python / ts)
- Authentication options: API keys, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS
- Sandbox environment setup and CI secret best practices
- Redwood Optimize: batching, KV/cache, quantization profiles
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for latency and cost

00:00:00 Maya (AE): "All right hi everyone, welcome, thanks for making time. I'm Maya from Redwood — I'll run through the quick plan, Carlos will dive into the SDK and sandbox, and then we'll show a couple optimize knobs. Uh, if you have questions ping in chat or interrupt. Lena, you want to give 30 seconds on your priorities?"

00:00:18 Lena (Lead ML Eng): "Yeah thanks Maya. Our main thing is: we want predictable latency for inference, we have high token QPS for the lab, and, um, we need to make sure we can own keys and audit logs for PCI-ish workflows. Also curious about hosting options — hosted vs dedicated vs private."

00:00:35 Omar (Platform): "And from infra we care about how keys are rotated, KMS integration, and if we can pin models in dedicated pools. Also CI/CD secrets flow — we can't put long lived API keys in repo."

00:00:50 Maya: "Great — we'll cover all of that. Carlos, over to you for the SDK quickstart."

00:01:05 Carlos (SE): "Cool thanks. I'm going to share my screen and show a Python quickstart — pip install redwood-sdk, then the minimal code snippet. Note: in some transcriptions it shows 'redwood-client' but the package is 'redwood-sdk'."

00:01:28 [screen share start — terminal]
00:01:33 Carlos: "So python -m venv venv && pip install redwood-sdk. Then from redwood import RedwoodClient, client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']). For TS it's: npm i @redwood/sdk and const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })."

00:02:10 Lena: "Quick q — what about SSO? We don't want to bake keys into env for CI."

00:02:16 Carlos: "Good question. For CI we recommend short-lived tokens issued via our CLI/OAuth flow. For enterprise you can enable SAML/SSO and mint scoped tokens with RBAC. There's also a recommended pattern using your KMS to encrypt the token in CI and decrypt at runtime. We have a docs page I'll drop after the call."

00:02:45 Priya (Security): "Can you call out audit logs and retention? We need 12 months and immutability for certain events."

00:02:52 Maya: "Yes, we support audit logs in the Private and Dedicated tiers; hosted has audit trails for API requests and token-level metadata but for longer immutability Private with your own log sink is typical. SOC2 report and logging details — I'll share the link."

00:03:10 Carlos: "Also note, 'KV cash' — sorry 'KV cache' — is our in-memory prefix cache that helps lower latencies for repeated context. It's transparent to the SDK but you can configure TTL and scope (per-model or global)."

00:03:34 [brief crosstalk]
00:03:40 Omar: "If we go Dedicated, can we pin a model family and quantization profile?"

00:03:47 Carlos: "Yes — Dedicated pools can pin model versions and runtime configs. You can also configure quantization profiles per-pool. There is an Optimize report that recommends quantization levels based on your prompt distributions. We ran one for another customer with similar token length distribution and recommended int8 for the decoder which saved ~40% per-token cost with a small quality delta."

00:04:20 Lena: "Nice. Can you show the Optimize UI?"

00:04:27 Carlos: "Sure — switching to the console: The Optimize tab shows suggested batching window, KV cache hit rate, and a recommended quantization profile. It also simulates cost impact if you adjust batch size or enable KV cache. For example, for small prompts the tool recommends reducing max_batch_wait_ms to keep p95 latency under 120ms."

00:05:10 [screenshot: Optimize dashboard]
00:05:18 Carlos: "There is also a downloadable CSV with per-route cost breakdowns and token accounting; that's what we usually share during pilot."

00:05:35 Priya: "About encryption — can we bring our own key (BYOK) for at-rest model caches and logs?"

00:05:42 Maya: "Yes. For Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSMs for on-prem. For hosted we have managed keys but we can do BYOK for enterprise contracts. I'll include the KMS integration guide."

00:06:05 [pause]
00:06:20 Carlos: "Back to SDK: quick demo of streaming responses. In Python you can iterate over response.stream() and get token deltas. Example snippet. Streaming uses server-sent events under the hood — sometimes the client libs show partial tokens and your UI can append."

00:06:40 Omar: "Does streaming impact billing or caching?"

00:06:44 Carlos: "Billing is token-based as usual. Streaming is orthogonal to caching, but KV cache reduces tokens emitted by avoiding recomputing prefix. If you stream and use caching, you'll often see fewer tokens overall."

00:07:05 Lena: "We plan to run a benchmark — mostly short replies with a 300-400 token context and 60-120 token responses at 15 QPS. Any recommended settings?"

00:07:16 Carlos: "For that workload the common pattern is: small batch size (1-4), enable KV cache for repeated prefixes if applicable, and set max_concurrency to match your pool size. On Optimize, we'd recommend 'latency-first' routing policy in hosted or reserve Dedicated capacity to get consistent p95. Also you can set a fallback policy to a cheaper quantized model for non-critical requests."

00:07:45 Maya: "If you want consistent p95, Dedicated or Private is the path; hosted is fine but there is more tail variability during noisy neighbor events, though our smart routing helps."

00:08:05 Priya: "How about data residency? We have EU customers."

00:08:09 Maya: "We have region options for hosted and Dedicated in NA/EU/APAC. Private gives you full control over residency. We'll capture the region requirement in the follow-up."

00:08:30 [02m mark on call — skipped ahead in transcript for demo pacing]

00:08:36 Carlos: "Switching to TypeScript quick example: shows environment.example file with REDWOOD_API_KEY and recommended usage for CI — use high-level SDK helper to fetch ephemeral tokens if SSO is enabled."

00:09:02 Lena: "One subtlety: our infra uses HashiCorp Vault for secrets. Any pre-built integration?"

00:09:08 Carlos: "We don't have an out-of-the-box Vault plugin, but the pattern is standard: store the short-lived token in Vault and have the CI job retrieve it at runtime. On Private you can run the Redwood node behind your VPC and use Vault with internal network."

00:09:28 Omar: "About IP allowlists and egress — can we restrict outbound traffic?"

00:09:33 Maya: "Yes, with Private deployments you control egress and can place nodes in your VPC. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and IP allowlist options for control plane communications. We'll note the network architecture diagram in the follow-up."

00:09:55 [small laugh]

00:10:03 Carlos: "Okay let's do a short live run. I'm going to call the sandbox endpoint with a sample prompt set that Lena uploaded to the shared spreadsheet. Expect raw latency numbers: cold start was earlier around 180ms but warm p50 ~35ms on the sandbox. Note: sandbox doesn't reflect a fully provisioned Dedicated pool."

00:10:28 [demo request sent]
00:10:33 Carlos: "Response streamed back — tokens coming in. You can see the response arrives in chunks, finalization at 120ms for this single threaded call. That's an optimistic number; we'll run a proper benchmark next week."

00:10:55 Lena: "Nice. Do you support per-token costs and token-level breakouts for internal chargebacks?"

00:11:02 Maya: "Yes, Console has token-level accounting by route and by API key; you can export to CSV and integrate into your chargeback buckets. We also provide per-request metadata so you can attach biz-unit tags."

00:11:20 Omar: "Any rate limiting patterns to prevent accidental spikes?"

00:11:25 Carlos: "We have customer-side recommended throttles and server-side quotas. You can set per-key rate limits and alarms. For high QPS consider Dedicated with auto-scaling thresholds."

00:11:45 Priya: "Regulatory question: does Redwood store prompts and outputs? We need to ensure PII is not retained in hosted logs."

00:11:54 Maya: "By default hosted will keep request logs for 30 days for debugging; retention is configurable. For PII-sensitive workloads you should use Private or redact at the app layer. We can also enable log redaction and token-level hashing. Again, docs will be shared."

00:12:18 [pause]

00:12:35 Carlos: "Now, a quick note on SDK error handling best practices: use exponential backoff, idempotency tokens for retrying non-streaming requests, and graceful fallback to cheaper model variant. We'll paste a sample retry decorator into the ticket."

00:12:56 Lena: "Is there an SDK retry built-in?"

00:13:00 Carlos: "Yes, both the Python and TS clients provide a config object for retry policy and max attempts. The default is conservative."

00:13:15 Maya: "Let's talk pricing briefly. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is a commit plus usage; Private is license + support. We'll send a tailored quote after you confirm target QPS and region."

00:13:31 Lena: "Can you provide sample numbers for Dedicated baseline?"

00:13:35 Maya: "General guidance: Dedicated starts at X GPUs for baseline — I won't read the contract numbers here but we'll attach the example pricing sheet. For our previous customer with similar scale, switching to int8 saved ~0.4x cost on token ops."

00:13:58 [15m mark note — discussion continued]

00:14:05 Omar: "Technical deep dive: how does batching interact with p95 latency? If we increase batch size to save cost, do we see p95 blow up?"

00:14:13 Carlos: "Yes there is a tradeoff. Optimize tool simulates this: increasing batch size reduces tokens per request cost but adds queue time. For a latency-first SLO you choose smaller batches and possibly increase pool capacity to keep both latency and cost in control. You can also set per-route batching policy."

00:14:40 Lena: "Can we limit which teams use which models to control spend?"

00:14:45 Maya: "Yes RBAC + per-route limits let you do that. For example, you can create a role that only calls a cheaper model and assign it to service accounts."

00:15:02 Priya: "Question on compliance audits: do you provide evidence of key rotation events and access logs?"

00:15:08 Maya: "Yes we provide logfile exports including token issuance events, user activity logs, and KMS integration proofs. For Private we can forward logs to your SIEM."

00:15:28 Carlos: "All right quick troubleshooting note: sometimes CLI shows an error '401 SAMEL mismatch' — that's a transcription thing, actual error is SAML assertion error; double-check issuer URL in the IdP config."

00:15:50 [laughter]

00:16:00 Maya: "Ok let's capture next steps — we discussed a benchmark for Nov 28. Carlos will provision sandbox and Maya will send docs. Any blockers?"

00:16:10 Lena: "No blockers. We just need the sandbox creds and the doc pack."

00:16:18 Omar: "Also can you give an example of the CI flow using ephemeral tokens and Vault? A tiny script?"

00:16:25 Carlos: "Yes I'll attach a sample in the ticket — small wrapper that calls 'redwood auth exchange' and writes a short-lived token to the env."

00:16:40 [brief pause, background noise, someone shuffles papers]

00:16:52 Priya: "One more — is there a data plane separation if we choose Dedicated? We need control plane outside our infra and data plane inside."

00:16:59 Maya: "You can choose Private for full control, or Dedicated with optional data plane isolation where inference nodes run in your VPC and control plane remains managed. We'll diagram both."

00:17:20 [time jump — demo wrap-up]

00:17:27 Carlos: "Wrapping up the SDK: we'll include the following snippets in the shared repo — python stream example, ts streaming, retry config, ephemeral token helper, and a sandbox env.example."

00:17:45 Lena: "Perfect. Also curious about model rollout — how do you do canary?"

00:17:50 Maya: "Console supports canary and A/B rollout; you can route a % to new model. If quality drops we'll auto-fallback to previous. There's also metric hooks for eval sets to trigger rollback."

00:18:10 Omar: "What telemetry does the SDK emit?"

00:18:13 Carlos: "SDK emits basic client-side metrics: request durations, retry counts, and optional debug traces you can enable. We also provide server-side traces per-request. You control PII scrubbing."

00:18:30 [22m mark — notes and Q&A]

00:18:35 Priya: "How long would a Private deployment take?"

00:18:38 Maya: "Typical timelines: Dedicated ~4–6 weeks for provisioning and network setup depending on region; Private (on-prem) usually 2–3 months for packaging and security reviews. We'll work with your infra team."

00:18:55 Lena: "For the benchmark next week, will you provision a Dedicated-like pool to emulate production?"

00:19:02 Carlos: "We can provision a larger sandbox instance with similar CPU/GPU mix to approximate Dedicated behavior, but it won't be identical. For final acceptance tests we recommend a short Dedicated commit or a performance POC where we provision actual Dedicated nodes."

00:19:20 Maya: "Ok, let's recap action items and owners. I'll also open a ticket in your CRM and attach the sample code and docs."

00:19:33 [closing remarks]
00:19:36 Maya: "Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the links and schedule the Nov 28 benchmark. Anything else?"

00:19:42 Lena: "Nothing further, thanks. Good session.

00:19:45 Omar: "Thanks all.

00:19:47 Priya: "Thanks.

00:19:50 [call ends]

Notes about transcription: There are a few OCR-like artifacts (SAMEL, KV cash) and occasional speaker label flips early in the file; audio quality medium. The timestamps in the transcript are approximate and not a verbatim minute-by-minute log but capture the main exchanges and demos.

References to shared artifacts and links included above.
